extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, agency counsel, policymakers, and members of the public seeking access to agency information
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements (amendment to APA §3) specifying what agency information must be published or made available to the public, procedure for requesting records, required indexes and vote records, enumerated exemptions, and judicial remedies and limits. Useful for agencies implementing disclosure obligations and for requesters and courts assessing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Federal Register (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register for the guidance of the public certain information (see subitems A–E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute requires agencies to publish specified categories of information in the Federal Register 'separately' and 'currently' for public guidance. It includes an exception that no person shall be required to resort to or be adversely affected by matter required to be published in the Federal Register and not so published, except when the person has actual and timely notice. Matter reasonably available to the affected class may be deemed published when incorporated by reference with approval of the Director of the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication: descriptions of central and field organization and public contact points (subitem A)
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Descriptions of its central and field organization and the established places at which, the officers from whom, and the methods whereby, the public may secure information, make submittals or requests, or obtain decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must describe organizational structure and provide concrete contact points and methods (places, officers, procedures) where the public can obtain information, submit materials, or get decisions. This must be published in the Federal Register for public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication: statements of general course and method of functions (subitem B)
rubrics_metrics.description: (B) Statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined, including the nature and requirements of all formal and informal procedures available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must describe how decisions are made and the formal and informal procedures available, including requirements and nature of those procedures, to guide public expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication: rules, forms, and instructions (subitem C)
rubrics_metrics.description: (C) Rules of procedure, descriptions of forms available or the places at which forms may be obtained, and instructions as to the scope and contents of all papers, reports, or examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publish procedural rules, availability/location of forms, and instructions on required scope and contents of filings, reports, or examinations so the public can comply with procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication: substantive rules, policies, and interpretations (subitem D)
rubrics_metrics.description: (D) Substantive rules of general applicability adopted as authorized by law, and statements of general policy or interpretations of general applicability formulated and adopted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive rules and general policies/interpretations that apply broadly must be published; this prevents reliance on undisclosed rules or policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication: amendments, revisions, or repeals (subitem E)
rubrics_metrics.description: (E) Every amendment, revision, or repeal of the foregoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When any of the listed materials (organization descriptions, procedures, rules, policies, etc.) are amended, revised, or repealed, agencies must publish those changes in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency opinions and orders (availability requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall, in accordance with published rules, make available for public inspection and copying (A) all final opinions (including concurring and dissenting opinions) and all orders made in the adjudication of cases, (B) those statements of policy and interpretations which have been adopted by the agency and are not published in the Federal Register, and (C) administrative staff manuals and instructions to staff that affect any member of the public, unless such materials are promptly published and copies offered for sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publish or make available final adjudicative opinions/orders, adopted policies/interpretations not in the Federal Register, and staff manuals/instructions that affect the public. If materials are promptly published and sold, separate availability may be unnecessary. Agencies must also maintain a current index identifying such matters issued after the Act's effective date; unpublished matters cannot be relied upon against private parties unless indexed and made available or the party had actual and timely notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction for privacy in published opinions/materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent required to prevent a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, an agency may delete identifying details when it makes available or publishes an opinion, statement of policy, interpretation, or staff manual or instruction: Provided that in every case the justification for the deletion must be fully explained in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redactions for privacy are permitted but must be narrowly tailored to prevent a 'clearly unwarranted' invasion of personal privacy, and any deletion must be justified in writing each time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency index requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall maintain and make available for public inspection and copying a current index providing identifying information for the public as to any matter which is issued, adopted, or promulgated after the effective date of this Act and which is required by this subsection to be made available or published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must keep a current, publicly available index that identifies items subject to the availability/publication requirements; failure to index bars reliance against private parties unless they had actual and timely notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on relying upon unpublished materials against private parties
rubrics_metrics.description: No final order, opinion, statement of policy, interpretation, or staff manual or instruction that affects any member of the public may be relied upon, used or cited as precedent by an agency against any private party unless it has been indexed and either made available or published as provided by this subsection or unless that private party shall have actual and timely notice of the terms thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects private parties from being bound by unpublished or unindexed agency materials unless they were indexed and available or the party had actual notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency records: availability upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Except with respect to the records made available pursuant to subsections (a) and (b), every agency shall, upon request for identifiable records made in accordance with published rules stating the time, place, fees to the extent authorized by statute and procedure to be followed, make such records promptly available to any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must conform to published rules (time, place, applicable fees, procedures). Agencies must promptly provide identifiable records not covered by (a) or (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial remedy for withholding agency records
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon complaint, the district court of the United States in the district in which the complainant resides, or has his principal place of business, or in which the agency records are situated shall have jurisdiction to enjoin the agency from the withholding of agency records and to order the production of any agency records improperly withheld from the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters may sue in district court where they reside, have principal place of business, or where records are located. The court can enjoin withholding and order production.

rubrics_metrics.name: De novo review and burden on the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: In such cases the court shall determine the matter de novo and the burden shall be upon the agency to sustain its action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District courts review the agency's withholding de novo (fresh review), and the agency bears the burden of justifying nondisclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contempt and expedited proceedings for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of noncompliance with the court's order, the district court may punish the responsible officers for contempt. Except as to those causes which the court deems of greater importance, proceedings before the district court as authorized by this subsection shall take precedence on the docket over all other causes and shall be assigned for hearing and trial at the earliest practicable date and expedited in every way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may hold agency officers in contempt for failing to comply; FOIA-type cases get docket priority and expedited handling unless the court finds other cases more important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency proceedings: vote records availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency having more than one member shall keep a record of the final votes of each member in every agency proceeding and such record shall be available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-member agencies must maintain and make available records of how each member voted on agency proceedings, enhancing transparency of decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 1: national defense or foreign policy secrets by Executive order
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters that are specifically required by Executive order to be kept secret in the interest of the national defense or foreign policy are not applicable to the disclosure provisions of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information classified by Executive order for national defense or foreign policy purposes is exempt from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 2: internal personnel rules and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters related solely to the internal personnel rules and practices of any agency are not subject to disclosure under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal-only personnel policies/practices that do not affect the public are excluded from disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 3: specifically exempted by statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters specifically exempted from disclosure by statute are not applicable to the disclosure provisions of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where another statute explicitly provides an exemption from disclosure, that statutory exemption controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 4: trade secrets and confidential commercial/financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from any person and privileged or confidential are exempt from disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietary, privileged, or confidential business information is protected from disclosure under this exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 5: inter-agency or intra-agency memorandums not available in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-agency or intra-agency memorandums or letters which would not be available by law to a private party in litigation with the agency are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberative, privileged, or other internal communications that a private party could not obtain in litigation are excluded from required disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 6: personnel and medical files where disclosure would invade privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel and medical files and similar files the disclosure of which would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal privacy interests in personnel and medical records can justify withholding where disclosure would be a 'clearly unwarranted' invasion of privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 7: investigatory files compiled for law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory files compiled for law enforcement purposes are exempt except to the extent available by law to a private party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law-enforcement investigatory files may be withheld subject to any statutory rights a private party may have to obtain such records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 8: examination, operating, or condition reports for financial institution regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Information contained in or related to examination, operating, or condition reports prepared by, on behalf of, or for the use of any agency responsible for the regulation or supervision of financial institutions is exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive supervisory reports about financial institutions prepared for regulators are excluded from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption 9: geological and geophysical information concerning wells
rubrics_metrics.description: Geological and geophysical information and data (including maps) concerning wells are exempt from disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietary geological/geophysical well data (including maps) is protected from release under this exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of exemptions (no broader withholding authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section authorizes withholding of information or limiting the availability of records to the public except as specifically stated in this section, nor shall this section be authority to withhold information from Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies cannot use this section as a general license to withhold information beyond the enumerated exemptions, and disclosure obligations do not permit withholding from Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: private party
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this section, 'private party' means any party other than an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who is protected by restrictions on relying upon unpublished materials: any non-agency entity/person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: This amendment shall become effective one year following the date of the enactment of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory lead time before these disclosure and indexing requirements become effective.
